run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T15:45:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a dependency failure: the cart service cannot reach its Redis backend because the valkey-cart pod's container was OOMKilled and is now in CrashLoopBackOff, so cart returns errors on AddItem/GetCart/EmptyCart; frontend's client spans to those cart operations carry error status, and frontend's own error-span rate rose from 0 to >0 starting at 15:45:00, matching the alert start 2026-11-16T15:45:07Z. Evidence chain: (a) frontend error spans in the 15m ending 16:03:54 total about 443 span-increases, led by grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (76.86) and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (42.33) client spans; (b) cart's own server spans carry the matching errors (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 76.86, GetCart 55.25, EmptyCart 1.11), while cart's Redis client spans HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE show no error series; (c) cart container logs say "Wasn't able to connect to redis" (140 matching lines in the window) and "Connection failed. Disposing the object"; (d) cart's VALKEY_ADDR is valkey-cart:6379 and the valkey-cart Service has no ready endpoint addresses because pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is not ready; (e) that pod's container has restartCount 4, is waiting in CrashLoopBackOff, and its last termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 15:48:06; kubelet BackOff events for it start at 15:45:05 (22 occurrences to 15:52:23), and the valkey-cart Deployment reports MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 15:48:06. The Deployment sets only 10Mi memory limit / 4Mi request for valkey, which is the strongest configuration candidate for the OOM; the exact memory value at the OOM instant is not verifiable (cadvisor peak recorded about 5.58MB, below the limit). Alternatives checked and not supported as the cause: flagd (no cart flag-evaluation error spans, flagd pod ready with 0 restarts, no flagd error series), node-level memory pressure (all 5 nodes Ready with MemoryPressure False, and valkey-cart is the only OOMKilled pod among 72), and a cart rollout/restart (cart pod running/ready with 0 restarts; its failures are logged as Redis connectivity). checkout also shows its own errors concentrated on its cart client calls and PlaceOrder, consistent with the same downstream cause; frontend-proxy ingress error spans rose coincidentally but its tie to this cause is temporal only. Important limits: no RequestErrorRate rule exists in Prometheus, Jaeger holds no spans after 15:24:08, trace-derived metrics stop around 15:55:00, and the frontend and valkey-cart container logs were empty to the tooling.

claims.text: Frontend emitted error spans in the 15 minutes ending 2026-11-16T16:03:54Z: about 443 span-increase in total, dominated by client spans grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (76.86), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (42.33), grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (23.39) and span GET (8.91), plus HTTP route spans such as GET /api/cart (42.33) and POST /api/cart (76.86).

Frontend error-span activity began at the alert time: sum of frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase over 2m was 0 at every step from 15:21 to 15:44, first non-zero 13.27 at 15:45:00, then 53.3 (15:47), 432 (15:49) and 227.2 at the series' last sample 15:55:00.

The cart service itself returned errors on its own server spans in the 15m ending 16:03:54Z: POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 76.86, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 55.25, POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.11, against totals of 305.22, 492.84 and 76.86 spans respectively; cart's Redis client spans HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE and its flagd ResolveBoolean client spans had no error series.

Cart container logs in the window contain repeated "Wasn't able to connect to redis" lines (140 matches between 15:40:00 and 16:03:54, newest 40 shown from 15:51:12 to 15:52:30) and, earlier in the window, "Connection failed. Disposing the object" together with "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." lines from 15:49:38 onward.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is the cart Redis backend and is unhealthy: container valkey-cart ready=false, restartCount=4, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 1m20s restarting failed container"), lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, startedAt 15:47:55Z and finishedAt 15:48:06Z; the pod's container spec sets memory limit 10Mi and request 4Mi.

Kubelet events for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft show BackOff "restarting failed container valkey-cart" 22 occurrences from 2026-11-16T15:45:05Z to 15:52:23Z, and container Created/Started events 6 occurrences from 15:07:35Z to 15:49:41Z.

Deployment valkey-cart (1 replica) reports Available=False, reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 2026-11-16T15:48:06Z with unavailableReplicas=1; its pod template sets the valkey-cart container to memory limit 10Mi / request 4Mi and cpu 10m/2m, while Deployment cart (image demo:2.1.3-cart, 165Mi limit) is Available=True with 1 ready replica.

The valkey-cart Service (Endpoints) currently has no ready addresses: addresses is empty and notReadyAddresses contains 100.96.5.138 targeting pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft; the cart Deployment's environment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and FLAGD_HOST=flagd, so cart's Redis traffic is directed at that unresolved Service.

Across 72 pods cluster-wide, only valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft has an OOMKilled last termination (exit 137, 4 restarts); the other 20 pods in namespace otel-demo are Running and ready with 0 restarts, while kube-system pods kube-apiserver-i-0f646caed8aca795a (restartCount 1) and kube-controller-manager-i-0f646caed8aca795a (restartCount 3) had last reason Error.

All 5 nodes report Ready=True and MemoryPressure=False (reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory), DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False at query time, i.e. no node-level memory pressure was visible when the objects were read.

checkout shows its own error spans in the 15m ending 16:03:54Z concentrated on cart calls and PlaceOrder: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 13.37 client-span errors, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.11, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 23.39 server-span errors and HTTP POST 10.03, out of PlaceOrder totals of 100.26 spans.
frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans rose from small pre-onset values (1.28 at 15:29, 1.33 at 15:37, 2 at 15:41, 4 at 15:45) to 33.3 at 15:47:07, 138.7 at 15:49:07 and 126.7 at 15:55:00.

Other services did not show comparable errors in Prometheus over the 78-minute window: payment's GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect error series were 0, ad's flagd ResolveBoolean error series was 0 (ad's flagd EventStream had a small 2.04 increase), and no error series was returned for flagd, product-catalog or currency in that query.

The recorded cgroup high-water marks do not show the valkey container reaching its 10Mi limit: over 14:45-16:03Z container_memory_max_usage_bytes for container valkey-cart peaked at 5,582,848 bytes (about 5.3MiB), container_memory_usage_bytes peaked at 4,079,616 bytes and the pod-level cgroup at 7,229,440 bytes, all below 10,485,760 bytes. So 'cgroup limit exceeded' is not directly demonstrated by these metrics, even though the kubelet/CRI reports OOMKilled exit 137 as the termination reason.

Primary causal chain: the valkey-cart Redis pod is OOMKilled and crash-looping (CrashLoopBackOff, 4 restarts, BackOff events from 15:45:05Z), so its Service publishes no ready endpoints; the cart service's gRPC handlers that need Redis (AddItem, GetCart, EmptyCart) then fail and are logged as "Wasn't able to connect to redis"; frontend's client spans to those cart operations carry error status, which raised frontend's error rate above 0 at 15:45 and triggered RequestErrorRate. Operation-level counts line up across services (AddItem 76.86 frontend client vs 76.86 cart server; cart GetCart 55.25 server vs 42.33 frontend client plus 13.37 checkout client), which supports the call-path link without proving it from a complete trace graph.

Configuration cause inside the Deployment: Deployment valkey-cart requests only 4Mi and limits only 10Mi of memory (cpu 2m/10m) for valkey 8.1.3, far below a Redis/Valkey server's normal working size; that undersized limit is the most likely reason the container is repeatedly OOM-killed. Because the cgroup high-water mark recorded by cadvisor stayed below 10Mi, the exact moment-of-kill memory value remains unverified, so this stays a hypothesis rather than a proven mechanism.

Rejected: a flagd failure behind the cart errors. Cart's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans show no error series in the 15m window, flagd pod flagd-6b4759757b-9j556 is Running with both containers ready and 0 restarts, and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for service flagd at all.

Rejected: node-level memory pressure killing workloads. All 5 nodes report MemoryPressure=False and Ready=True, and among all 72 pods in the cluster only valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft has an OOMKilled last termination, so a broad node OOM event is not supported (node conditions and pod objects were read after the incident window, at about 16:04-16:05Z).

Rejected: the cart service itself crashed or was rolled out during the incident. cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and the cart Deployment is Available=True, while cart's own logs attribute its request failures to Redis connectivity ("Wasn't able to connect to redis", "Connection failed. Disposing the object").

gaps: Prometheus holds no rule named RequestErrorRate: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data (852d4dd3-9a7a-4481-a4e7-2057d6fd60dd-t0:7f86900e-cfd7-4947-b312-da945e7c95f7) and a full rule listing also returned no_data (4acd04a5-58e7-47cf-be48-a2d43e75c472-t0:35a7f452-0f27-4ea0-8a7f-cd19c7f01c4f), so the alert's exact expression and whether it is still firing could not be verified.

Jaeger returned no traces after 2026-11-16T15:24:08Z: cart trace search ended at source_end_at 15:24:08 (153e5335-9f7d-4e19-8b42-b117d423442b-t0:067a4c03-eecd-49c1-8df2-b62b3ee46c31, incomplete), and frontend searches returned no_data for 15:50-16:03 (60a3efcd-6b8a-4615-8f25-af889a171341-t0:8fc961a6-d4b3-4f27-8baf-95594aeae852) and no match for error=true on cart (f0c3b2ae-2365-466b-b3ae-373445578389-t0:ae02b582-aa57-4832-93e1-63a0193d4e8f), so per-span error details for the incident window are unavailable.

The frontend pod's application logs contained no lines for 15:40-16:03Z: both a filtered read (fd6273d7-7f99-4a10-875a-aa7373fc7522-t1:3be68c0f-661c-43ca-aeef-022445b892d8, status no_data) and an unfiltered read (6b3350f1-e99d-4785-b70f-b1572c40e242-t0:5fe73db5-c1c8-4772-ac46-7e0e1bccbd4a, status no_data) returned 0 lines, so frontend's own error logging could not be examined.

Container logs of pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft returned no lines (1ac74cbc-5ab2-4d6f-b21e-281227167b0d-t0:4d140eec-13f6-459c-afaa-8fd05aa3ceb5, status no_data) and its previous container instance was unavailable, so the Redis-side shutdown/OOM message is unknown.

Trace-derived series stop at about 15:55:00Z (data_as_of 15:55:00 for the frontend error series), so frontend/cart error state from 15:55 to 16:03:54 is unknown; and Jaeger span data ends at 15:24:08.

The exact memory value at the OOM kill is unverified: cadvisor high-water marks (container max 5,582,848 bytes, pod cgroup 7,229,440 bytes) are below the 10Mi limit, so whether the cgroup limit was exceeded or another memory-pressure mechanism selected the container cannot be settled from this data.

Node conditions, pod and Service objects were read after the window (about 16:04-16:05Z), so the cluster state during 15:45-15:55Z is not directly observed; individual valkey container restart timestamps before the first BackOff event at 15:45:05Z are not available.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so it could not be checked whether the valkey-cart memory limit or any manifest changed near the incident window.

A flagd log read returned no lines (b8fe8fef-3791-44c2-929a-7bce56f7d57b-t1:8f27fa48-1758-45cc-8404-133a9e3c03fa, status no_data), so flagd health rests on pod status and span metrics rather than its logs.

Services with no error series (accounting, currency, email, shipping, quote, product-catalog, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, recommendation, fraud-detection) are unknown rather than confirmed error-free, since a missing series is not a zero value.
next_steps: Raise Deployment valkey-cart's memory request/limit from 4Mi/10Mi to a size appropriate for valkey (hundreds of MiB) and confirm the OOMKilled/CrashLoopBackOff cycle stops; this is advisory only and was not executed.
Read the valkey-cart container's stdout/stderr directly on node i-0d211959f7bf532cd (kubectl logs / node journal), since the log API returned no lines, to capture the Redis-side OOM/shutdown message.

Verify in the alerting rule store (not visible in this Prometheus) the RequestErrorRate expression and whether counting frontend client spans to dependencies is intended, since the alert reflects a dependency failure rather than a frontend-internal fault.
Add a specific alert or monitor on valkey-cart pod readiness, restart count and OOMKilled terminations so a Redis dependency crash pages before frontend error rate crosses its threshold.

Confirm whether the pre-existing 1-4 per 2m frontend-proxy ingress error spans (15:29-15:45) and ad's flagd EventStream errors (2.04 increase over 78m) are known baseline noise or need separate follow-up.
